main_text.l: DE RATIONALI VIRTVTE ORGANICA.
PROPOSITIO I.
Organicas virtutes eas dicimus, quæ occupatur
in rectè apparandis Instrumentis, ad discipli-
nas assequendas à natura nobis attributis.
II.
Duo verò hæc sunt[?], ORATIO & RATIOCINA-
TIO: quibus ut quomodo natura utimur, ita longè
tutius & rectius arte. Cicero in lib.Orat.
III.
Quòd si igitur in sola Oratione fuerint occupata;
pariunt illa GRAMMATICAM, benè loquendi ar-
tificio contentam.
IV.
Si verò in sola Ratiocinatione, LOGICAM, nobi-
le instrumentum dextrè philosophandi, & in Philo-
sophia verum à falso distinguendi.
V.
Si autem in utrisq; simul versentur, RHETORI-
CAM, facultatem ornatè copiosèq; dicendi proge-
nerant. Arist.Rhet.1.c.3 Alexand. in Præf. in lib.1. Top.
VI.
Et eiusdè[?] insuper colonias tres: ORATORIAM, HISTORICAM,
& POETICAM. Quæusus & fructus quidam esse iudicantur Logicarum artium ex-
ercendarum.
VII.
His igitur Instrumentis Philosophiæ universæ,
Theoricæ, Practicæ, sed & superiorū quoq; facultatū,
Medicinæ dico, Iurisprudentiæ & S.S.Theologiæ my-
steria, initiatis referantur, aperiuntur & patefiunt

page.notes: Drop cap "O" of the first paragraph is joined to "Organicas". "sunt" after "hæc" is partly obscured by a stray ink mark; read as "sunt" with [?]. "eiusdè" is faintly printed and uncertain. "Quæusus" and "ORATORIAM" are read as printed. The word "Gram-" at the foot is the catchword for the next page, not part of the text. Text is continuous from the previous page only in the sense that the page opens a new division; no running head or page number is printed.
